Subject: CorpStream discovery: sample prompts + redaction checklist & next steps

Hi Amit — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier today. High-level recap and concrete asks so we can move the eval forward: 

Summary of needs
- In-product assistant for customer support triage + policy routing (short answers + follow-up Qs).
- Real-time constraints: 90th pct latency target ~120ms token for interactive flows; batch async for nightly reports.
- Security: SOC2 + contractual data retention limits (30 days KV cache).

Model & eval pointers (initial recs)
- Candidate families: redwood-3b-opt (low-cost interactive), redwood-13b-q4f (best quality/cost balance), and redwood-34b-int8 (for heavy-context logs).
- We ran a quick benchmark on a 2k prompt sample — link to a short report attached and on Drive (see attachments + links).

Action items for CorpStream (requested by Apr 13)
1) Please upload 1–2 CSVs with representative user prompts (questions, follow-ups, edge cases) — use the attached sample-prompt-template.csv. Mark any rows that contain sensitive/special-handling content.
2) Flag categories that must be redacted (PII, account_numbers, proprietory snippets) and indicate whether you can pre-redact. If not, we will provide redaction guidance.
3) Share the business priority for short answers vs. long-form summaries (helps us pick prompt/temperature tuning).

Attachments: CorpStream_MA_Plan_Draft.pdf (proposal outline), sample-prompt-template.csv (CSV template)

Next meeting: can we target a 30–45 minute hands-on prompt intake workshop next week? Ben (SE) will run a short session to walk through the template and redaction steps.

Thanks — I’ll kick off an internal checklist and loop in Security for the SOC2 artifacts.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0118

Thanks Amit — received the CSV and that volume is perfect for an initial run. Below are a few specifics to keep things moving fast: 

Prompt formatting we prefer for rapid ingestion
- Columns: id, raw_user_text, context_snippets (optional), timestamp_utc, confidential_flag
- If you can pseudonymize emails/order_ids into consistent tokens (e.g. [EMAIL_1], [ORDER_23]) that helps model behavior and de-identification testing.

Redaction checklist (short) — attached redaction-checklist.md and pasted below: 1) Remove full SSNs and bank account numbers (replace with [SSN], [BANK_ACCT]);
2) Replace email addresses with [EMAIL_n] tokens, phone numbers with [PHONE_n];
3) Strip any full credit-card numbers;
4) For customer names, you can keep first names but flag as PII if that matters for your policy;
5) Remove any system API keys, protobuf dumps, or raw logs with tokens.

Model-choice guidance (quick):
- redwood-3b-opt: target if you want low-cost, conversational responses and can accept occasional factual gaps.
- redwood-13b-q4f: our recommended starting point for high-quality answer ranking at reasonable latency/cost — good fit for triage and routing.
- redwood-34b-int8: use for long-context summarization of support threads and end-of-day batch jobs.

Benchmarks & SLOs
- Our internal eval (linked) shows redwood-13b-q4f hitting ~110ms 90th token in an optimally provisioned Dedicated pool with batching disabled for interactive sessions.
- Cost ballpark (hosted): 0.8–1.2 cents per input+output token for the 13b family depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness. We’ll produce a more precise estimate once we see prompt length distribution.

Next steps
- Please upload a cleaned CSV by Tue Apr 13 if possible.
- Ben will schedule the workshop for Apr 14–15 (30 minutes) — he’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redaction-checklist.md

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk the redaction steps together.

—Michael
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Amit — quick technical note from the SE side before the workshop: 

1) Inference modes: for the interactive SLA you mentioned, we recommend starting with dedicated capacity and single-request routing (no large batching) to keep tail latency predictable.
2) Quantization: redwood-13b-q4f gives a good tradeoff; if you want lower cost we can try q4_0 or q4_k_mixed, but we should run a short A/B on quality-sensitive prompts.
3) KV cache policy: set to 30 days per your retention ask; we’ll instrument token-level cost and per-route latency in the console so you can watch regressions.

Cost/time estimate for eval pack
- Initial pass (run 820-row sample + 2k synthetic variants): 24–36 hours of run time on our Dedicated dev pool.
- Turnaround to share a model-fit report: ~3 business days after we get cleaned data.

I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute workshop 2027-04-14 10:00am PT (tentative). If that slot works, accept and I’ll include a short agenda: template walk-through, sample in/out, anonymization checklist.

—Ben
SE, Redwood Inference
